final_state.final_report:
MOCK: rule-based agent stand-ins; Python calculations are real.

Method: two-sided Welch independent-samples t-test  (data version v2; Python: scipy.stats.ttest_ind(group_1='treatment', group_2='control', equal_var=False, alternative='two-sided'); confidence_interval(confidence_level=0.95))
H0: Δ = 0 versus H1: Δ ≠ 0, where Δ = μ(group = treatment) − μ(group = control) for the mean of outcome; α = 0.05

| Group | n | Mean | SD |
|---|---|---|---|
| treatment | 25 | 1.22 | 0.69 |
| control | 25 | 3.95 | 20.03 |

Mean difference = -2.73 (95% CI -11.01 to 5.54); t(24.06) = -0.682; p = 0.5016
Decision at α = 0.05: do_not_reject_H0
Distribution checks (descriptive only, never used to choose the method): [{'check': 'shapiro_wilk', 'variable': 'outcome', 'group': 'treatment', 'n': 25, 'shapiro_wilk_p': 0.16838955839373165}, {'check': 'shapiro_wilk', 'variable': 'outcome', 'group': 'control', 'n': 25, 'shapiro_wilk_p': 2.1541308636409634e-10}]

The analysis included 25 records in group treatment and 25 in group control. Welch's test gave t(24.06) = -0.682, p = 0.5016. At alpha = 0.05, we do not reject H0. The estimated mean difference (treatment minus control) was -2.73 (95% CI -11.01 to 5.54). This is not evidence that there is no difference or association.

Limitations:
- Random allocation was not established. This analysis describes an association and does not establish causation.
- Inference is conditional on the stated independent observations and the method's distribution and model assumptions; descriptive checks do not prove these assumptions.
